subject: Re: Performance SLO p95/p99 - hosted API vs current provider - qualification follow-up
messages:
From: Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finlytics.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Rohit Kumar <rohit.kumar@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO recap (Finlytics / Redwood)

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to walk through where we're trying to get to. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying points so we can move to a qualification benchmark:

Summary of Finlytics requirements:
- End-to-end latency (client -> app -> LLM -> app -> client) targets (short prompts, <=128 tokens): p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 650ms.
- Longer responses / streaming (>=1024 tokens): p95 <= 900ms, p99 <= 1200ms (we care about tail behavior during streaming).
- Concurrency: expected sustained 100 concurrent active requests during peak; bursts to 300 for short windows.
- Throughput: baseline ~600 requests/minute across our regional pool.
- Typical payload: JSON request with metadata + prompt; median prompt length ~80 tokens, 95th ~720 tokens.

We attached our internal SLO doc (finlytics_slo_requirements.pdf). Our current provider reports p95 ~420ms and p99 ~900ms for short prompts — which is okay, but we want to validate whether Redwood hosted API can reliably hit our targets across traffic shapes, especially for streaming.

Next steps from our side: share a redacted trace / representative traffic profile if helpful. From Redwood: can you confirm the hosted API numbers you expect, and any config assumptions (batching, quantization, region)? Also would like to see a short step-by-step for running a fair benchmark and what data you need from us.

Thanks,
Sarah Lang
Director, ML Engineering
Finlytics

--
Attachment: finlytics_slo_requirements.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap (Finlytics / Redwood)

Sarah — appreciate the clear recap and the attached SLO doc. Confirming my understanding and listing the actions we propose to qualify p95/p99 for hosted API vs your current provider:

My read of your asks:
- Short prompts (<=128 tokens): p95 <=350ms, p99 <=650ms.
- Long/streaming (>=1024 tokens): p95 <=900ms, p99 <=1200ms.
- Sustained concurrency ~100, bursts to 300, throughput ~600 RPM.

Actions we suggest:
1) You share an anonymized traffic profile or a small set of representative traces (headers removed) — helps us reproduce tail behavior.
2) We run two runs in your target region (us-west):
   - Redwood hosted API baseline with our standard batching/kv-cache config.
   - Comparative run against a compatible model on your current provider (if you can share exact model & API call patterns) or we run a synthetic match to your profiles.
3) We'll provide a short summary: p50/p95/p99, concurrency curves, and notes on streaming chunk latency and rebuffer behavior.

A few clarification Qs:
- Do you require server-sent events style streaming (chunked tokens) or are you using polling for partial outputs?
- Any strict encryption/KMS constraints for test runs?

We can provision a hosted snapshot for you to validate — I'll attach a sample latency snapshot from internal runs (redwood_latency_snapshot_20261004.png) so you can see the kind of output you'll get.

Are you available for a 30-min follow-up on 2026-10-06 at 10:00 AM PT? If not, propose alternatives and we'll accommodate.

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finlytics.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO recap (Finlytics / Redwood)

Sarah — thanks for the doc and the clear numbers. We ran a quick internal validation (us-west region) to illustrate the delta you might expect from Redwood hosted API on a similar model at your short-prompt profile (<=128 tokens) with sustained concurrency ~100. High-level results (short prompts, median payload ~80 tokens):

Redwood hosted API (default runtime config, batching enabled, KV prefix cache warm):
- p50: 190ms
- p95: 280ms
- p99: 520ms
- Notes: concurrency test at 100 sustained; we used continuous batching window 20ms and max_batch_size 64 to keep latency predictable.

Finlytics' reported numbers (current provider, per your doc):
- p50: ~260ms
- p95: ~420ms
- p99: ~900ms

Streaming behaviour: for long responses we see the token-chunk latency dominated by generation time; for a 1024-token output with streaming enabled our median first-chunk latency stays <350ms but tail (p99) can stretch toward your 900-1200ms window depending on chunk size and SSE push intervals. We recommend a 64-token chunk size for best tradeoff of perceived latency vs throughput.

Caveats & assumptions:
- Tests used a 13B-class open model (we can re-run on your exact model if you provide the same weights/API endpoints).
- Network hops: these were end-to-end from a client VM in us-west to our hosted endpoint in us-west. If your app architecture adds proxies, please factor that in.
- Encryption/KMS: no special KMS used for the benchmark; we can re-run with customer-managed keys if required (will add small crypto overhead).

Next steps / Ask from Finlytics:
- Share a 10-minute sample trace and a small synthetic traffic file (1-2k requests) so we can run a like-for-like comparison.
- Confirm whether you're able to route a short test to Redwood hosted API or prefer we run a synthetic replay from our side.
- Confirm follow-up time — Aditya suggested 2026-10-06 10:00 AM PT; that works for us.

I'll attach the brief PDF with the run summary and raw metrics, and add a HubSpot note referencing this thread. Putting Dylan on cc to help scope any additional benchmarking resources.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
